bull.b: The Anthropic agreement materially improves long-term revenue visibility through a 20-year commitment and expands TeraWulf’s position in AI infrastructure. A large contracted deployment can support sustained capacity growth, customer credibility, and more predictable investment planning as phased capacity comes online.

HPC leasing is becoming a larger and faster-growing contributor than the company’s legacy bitcoin-mining focus. Continued revenue mix expansion toward contracted data-center services could improve business durability and reduce reliance on bitcoin production and its protocol-driven economics.

Substantial liquidity and the monetization of Abernathy provide funding for committed Lake Mariner investment and other expansion without an expected near-term equity raise. Recycling capital from a joint venture toward larger controlled assets can strengthen execution capacity and strategic focus.

bear.b: The company’s gross profitability has not translated into sustainable operating or net earnings, with severe TTM losses and negative adjusted EBITDA during continued expansion. Persistent cost burdens and pre-revenue spending could absorb the benefits of rising capacity unless margins improve as projects enter service.

Negative operating cash flow shows the core business is not currently self-funding, while deeply negative free cash flow reflects substantial ongoing investment and cash requirements. Continued burn increases dependence on liquidity, asset monetization, or financing to complete growth projects and meet obligations.

Very high debt relative to reported equity leaves limited capitalization support for a business still generating losses and funding large projects. This weakens financial flexibility and makes cash interest and refinancing demands more consequential, particularly while the company transitions toward scaled HPC operations.
